card.name: Farandole
card.era: Name attested from the 18th c.; practiced earlier
card.tagline: Open-chain community dance of Provence led by a leader.
card.profile: The farandole is an open-chain community dance of Provence in 6/8 time, in which dancers join hands (or link by handkerchief/ribbon) in a long line led by a leader who waves a flag and guides the chain through spirals, serpentines and arches (Wikipedia; Britannica). It is accompanied by the galoubet (a three-holed pipe) and the tambourin (a long Provencal tabor), both played by a single tambourinaire. Danced at major Provencal feasts (Corpus Christi; Tarascon's Tarasque festival) and embedded in the Provencal Christmas creche tradition. It resembles the gavotte, jig and tarantella; the Revolutionary carmagnole is a derivative.
card.insight: Bizet used a Provencal farandole tune in the finale of his 'L'Arlesienne' Suite No. 2 (arr. Guiraud, 1879), helping popularize the form in classical music (Encyclopedia.com / Concise Oxford Dictionary of Music).

observation.dancers: a mixed group of about 14 adults of various ages (both men and women)
observation.formation_and_space: a long line of dancers holding hands that circles around into a ring and later winds in a single-file procession
observation.posture: upright torso, soft knees with weight shifting on each step, upright and lively
observation.footwork: lively hopping and stepping on beat, alternating feet with light springy hops
observation.arms_and_hands: hands held in a chain holding hands with neighbors; at times arms raise up to form arches while others pass underneath
observation.hips_and_torso: minimal hip movement, torso remains upright and turns as the group circles
observation.partnering: hand-in-hand chain connection with all adjacent dancers throughout
observation.levels_jumps_turns: standing level with small springy hops, curving path travels in circle and snake-like patterns
observation.costume_and_props: traditional folk attire: women wear white caps, vests, striped skirts with aprons, and large round straw hats worn on their backs; men wear white trousers, patterned vests, dark jackets or shirts, and hats
